'''Eva Bayer-Fluckiger''' (born 25 June 1951) is a Hungarian and Swiss [[mathematician]]. She is a Professor Emeritus at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]]. She has worked on several topics in topology, algebra and number theory, e.g. on the theory of knots, on lattices, on quadratic forms and on [[Galois cohomology]]. Along with [[Raman Parimala]], she proved [[Serre's conjecture II (algebra)|Serre's conjecture II]] regarding the Galois cohomology of a simply-connected semisimple algebraic group  when such a group is of classical type.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Bayer-Fluckiger, E.|author2=Parimala, R.|title=Galois cohomology of the classical groups over fields of cohomological dimension&nbsp;≤&nbsp;2|journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]|year=1995|volume=122|pages=195&ndash;229|doi=10.1007/BF01231443|s2cid=124673233 }}</ref>

==Early life and career==
Bayer-Fluckiger was born in [[Budapest]], Hungary.<ref name=uni>{{cite web|url=https://www.uni-due.de/ekfg/evabayerfluckigermsm01.shtml|title=Prof. Dr. Eva Bayer-Fluckiger - Maria Sibylla Merian-Preisträgerin 2001|accessdate=14 May 2019}}</ref> She attended the [[University of Geneva]], where she obtained her [[doctorate]] under supervision of [[Michel Kervaire]] in 1978.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|53689}}</ref> She was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from 1983 to 1984. From 1990 to 1996, she was an executive committee member of the [[European Mathematical Society]]<ref>[https://www.ias.edu/scholars/eva-bayer-fluckiger Institute for Advanced Study: A Community of Scholars] Retrieved 14 May 2019.</ref> and since 2006 served on [[editorial board]] of its ''[[Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ems-ph.org/journals/journal.php?jrn=cmh|title=Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici|publisher=European Mathematical Society|accessdate=14 May 2019}}</ref>

==Awards==
In 2001, the Essen College of Gender Studies gave Bayer-Fluckiger their Maria Sibylla Merian Prize, "for her achievements in number theory".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uni-due.de/ekfg/prize.shtml|title=Maria Sibylla Merian-Prize|publisher=University of Duisburg-Essen|accessdate=18 Jun 2020}}</ref> She was Emmy Noether guest professor at the University of Göttingen in 2003. She was named a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]], in the 2022 class of fellows, "for contributions to number theory, algebra, and topology, and for service to the profession".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi|title=2022 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2021-11-05}}</ref>
